# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 9 (Bu-Vb Ss9)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Ss9
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Aññabhāgiya* rule, designated as Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 9 (*Bu-Vb Ss9*), belongs to the Vinaya Piṭaka's Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga [SuttaCentral]. The disciplinary rule establishes that a Buddhist monk who, driven by anger, uses an indirect pretext or ploy to falsely accuse a fellow monk of an offense entailing expulsion (*pārājika*) commits a grave infraction requiring formal suspension and rehabilitation by the Saṅgha (*saṅghādisesa*) [SuttaCentral]. The text is available in an English translation by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral]. None of the scanned secondary literature passages directly discuss this rule, as the search matches for "ss 9" correspond to unrelated section numbers in non-Vinaya texts, Tibetan grammar, or distinct monastic rules.
SuttaCentral identifies widespread parallels to the rule across all major early Buddhist traditions, including the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (*pli-tv-bu-pm-ss9*), the *Parivāra*, the Pali *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (*pli-tv-bi-vb-ss9*), and corresponding rules in the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya Vinaya lineages preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse computations by DharmaNexus reflect this continuity: internally, the rule shares its closest and most substantial textual overlap with the preceding groundless accusation rule, Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 8 ( Bu-Vb Ss8, 457 matches, over 38,000 shared characters, spanning §1.2.3–2.1.10) [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits significant text sharing with Vinaya procedural texts and commentaries, such as the *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Samathabheda* (Parivāra 5), the *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-purāṇa-ṭīkā*, and the *Samathakkhandhaka* (Khandhaka 14) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus cross-language alignments connect the Pali text to Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* sections (*D0003-2*, *D0003-3*), agreeing with SuttaCentral's curated parallel inventory [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
